fields.System.Title: INV-6 — Batches and expiry
fields.System.Description:
Purpose

Track stock by production batch and expiry date, so that dated goods are shipped in the right
order and a recall can find every affected unit.

Scope

In. Batch creation, batch queries, FEFO ordering, expiry blocking, expiring-stock reporting.

Out. Serial number tracking — that is [OUT-408](../../stories/OUT/OUT-408-capture-serial-numbers.md)
and [INB-211](../../stories/INB/INB-211-capture-serial-numbers.md), at Stage 4.

Design notes

Batches add a dimension to every quantity question. Stock is no longer "40 units in
location A" but "25 of batch B221 expiring in June and 15 of batch B240 expiring in September,
both in location A". Allocation, counting, and reporting all have to respect it.

FEFO must be applied at batch level, not location level. A location holding two batches
where the system picks "the location" will ship the wrong one, and the old batch expires
unsold.

Switching a product to batch-tracked after it has stock is genuinely hard — the existing
stock has no batch. Plan for the flag to be set at product creation and frozen afterwards, with
a documented manual procedure for the rare exception. See
[FDN-607](../../stories/FDN/FDN-607-freeze-fields.md).

Risks

| Risk | Reference |
|---|---|
| FEFO ignored for a mixed-batch location | [doc 09 §4.1](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Batch typed rather than scanned, with a typo | [doc 05 WF 1](../../../docs/05-workflows.md) |
| Only one batch counted in a multi-batch location | [doc 09 §6.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
| Returned stock restocked with the original expiry | [doc 09 §8.3](../../../docs/09-defect-hotspots.md) |
